test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 11 Feb 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following revolutionary freedom fighters was assassinated by Abdul Rashid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Shraddhanand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swami Shraddhanand**, also known as** Mahatma Munshi Ram Vij**, was an** Indian nationalist and Arya Samaj sannyasi **who spread **Dayananda Saraswati's teachings.**
 
• This includes the development of educational institutions such as the **Gurukul Kangri University**, as well as a vital part in the Hindu reform movements of the** Sangathan (consolidation and organization) and Shuddhi (purification)** in the 1920s.
 
• Shraddhanand left Gurukul in **1917 **to become a leader in** Hindu reform organizations** and the** Indian Independence struggle.**
 
• Swami Shradhanand was the only** Hindu Sanyasi **who addressed a huge gathering from the minarets of the** main Jama Masjid New Delhi, **for national solidarity and Vedic dharma starting his speech with the recitation of Ved mantras.
 
• He also** published newspapers** in two languages. He advocated** Hindi in the Devanagri script**, aided the poor, and encouraged **women's education.**
 
• Shraddhanand was named **"the greatest and most sincere champion of the Untouchables"** by** Dr. Ambedkar in 1922.**
 
• In late **1923,** he was elected president of the **Bhartiya Hindu Shuddhi Sabha**, which was founded with the goal of converting Muslims in the western United Province, particularly the **'Malkana Rajputs.'**
 
• To safeguard Hindu society from the** onslaught of Christianity and Islam's forced conversions,** he and the Arya Samaj launched the **'Shuddhi'** (purification) program, which aimed to reintegrate Christians and Muslims into Hindu society. During the 1920s, this resulted in a growing communalization of social life.
 
• As a result, **Abdul Rashid assassinated **him on **December 23, 1926.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BR Ambedkar**:

 
 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** was an Indian **jurist, economist, social reformer, and politician** who led the committee that drafted the Indian Constitution from the Constituent Assembly debates.
 
• He served as** **Law and Justice Minister in Jawaharlal Nehru's first cabinet and inspired the **Dalit Buddhist movement **after renouncing Hinduism.
 
• He was a firm believer in** individual liberty **and an outspoken** critic of caste society.**
 
• Ambedkar played a key role in the establishment of the **Reserve Bank of India in 1935**.
 
• The** Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 **was Ambedkar’s first important crusade.
 
• Ambedkar fought for **three years** to get the comprehensive **Hindu Code Bill passed** which gave several **important rights to women.**
 
 
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:**
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was an **Indian author, political activist, and freedom warrior**.
 
• He was a key figure in the** Indian independence struggle**.
 
• **Punjab Kesari **was his popular title.
 
• He was one of the **Lal Bal Pal triumvirate's three members**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was the first to say the iconic slogan** "Simon Go Back." **
 
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose:**
 
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose was a key figure in** India's freedom struggle.**
 
• He was a leader of the **Indian National Congress **and a participant in the **non-cooperation movement, **belonging to the more militant faction and advocating socialist ideals.
 
• He was given the title **'Netaji'** by Indian soldiers of the **Azad Hind Fauj in Germany in 1942.**
